published_prior_art.cite: GoblerWindischDrton2025 and PetersEtAl2014 require a common supplied vertex/group set for their nondescendant reduction.
GoblerWindischDrton2025 identifies a DAG for a supplied vector partition; WahlNinadRunge2024 identifies joint partition--graph learning as future work.
GoblerWindischDrton2025, Corollary 1 identifies the GANM DAG under its supplied-group Condition 1.
GoblerWindischDrton2025 supplies only fixed-partition DAG identification; no checked source identifies an innovation-atomic coordinate partition from P.
PetersEtAl2014, Theorem 28, and GoblerWindischDrton2025, Corollary 1, give the singleton and supplied-group reductions.
GutchTheis2012 supplies an irreducibility analogue, but not this nonlinear fixed-coordinate GANM merging witness.
HoyerEtAl2008 records linear-Gaussian directional reversibility; this is its grouped-target embedding.
RollandEtAl2022 provides score-based scalar ANM recovery, not degree completeness for arbitrary internal vector ANM splits.
No checked cited source gives a sound-and-complete unknown-partition GANM certificate; its claimed global completeness nevertheless has the scope defect flagged below.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 3 (atomic partition-and-DAG recovery)
novelty_flags.one_line: The strict-extension headline names only GoblerWindischDrton2025 as a direct comparator; Peters, Wahl, and Gutch are contextual rather than a second comparator or a proved generic-class frontier.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 4 (finite-dimensional certificate)
soundness_flags.one_line: Exact recovery of T(P) assumes A(P)=A_{r,s}, thereby assuming away every nonpolynomial competing representation; Open-ended Question 2 only concerns internal splits within polynomial representations and does not establish this load-bearing closure.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: GANMs are defined on a prespecified tuple of random-vector groups; Corollary 1 identifies the graph when every parent/group/nondescendant conditioning triple satisfies Condition 1.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 16, Definition 27, Theorem 28, Proposition 29; pp. 36-37, proofs
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Restricted ANMs plus causal minimality identify a shared-vertex DAG, and Proposition 29 constructs opposed edges with a nondescendant conditioning set for two different DAGs on that same vertex set.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, assumptions preceding Theorem 1; Theorem 1 and Corollary 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes strictly positive, three-times differentiable densities/functions for its differential analysis, derives the reverse-ANM differential restriction, and gives the linear-Gaussian reversible boundary.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Causal Inference 12 (2024), published version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states that learning pairs consisting of a partition and a graph over its constituents under suitable optimality constraints is an interesting but challenging future problem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the certificate's assumption A(P)=A_{r,s} with a proved representation-closure theorem, or restate the certificate exactly for T_{r,s}(P) so its completeness no longer assumes away nonpolynomial competitors.

Add an explicit strict-inclusion/frontier result against both supplied-group GANM identification and scalar restricted-ANM identification, or quantify over the generic class of all externally supplied partitions and prove the inclusion is strict.
State the polynomial degree-completeness route as two separate obligations: internal-split closure and competing-representation closure from a polynomial observed log-density.

recommended_next_step: Revise the certificate to avoid assumed global representation closure and strengthen the headline comparator chain before advancing the crossing-rigidity kernel.
